Embeddings are vector representations that encode semantic information from various data types, such as text, images, audio, and video.

This page outlines current approaches to embedding generation, including models, training algorithms, and benchmarks. It also covers data preparation strategies and specialized methods for domain-specific applications.
- **Trivial Approach:** Translate everything to English, then do stuff.

In the realm of embedding generation, various established techniques have been developed to create effective vector representations. These methods leverage different architectures, training strategies, and data types to enhance the quality and applicability of embeddings across diverse domains. Below, we explore some of the most prominent existing methods that have shaped the landscape of embedding models.

- **Contrastive Pre-training:** A self-supervised learning technique that trains models to differentiate between similar and dissimilar data pairs by maximizing the agreement between positive pairs while minimizing it for negative pairs. This approach is widely used to improve the quality of embeddings by leveraging large unlabeled datasets.

- **Fine-tuning:** A transfer learning technique that adapts pre-trained embedding models to specific domains or tasks by updating model parameters using task-specific data while preserving general knowledge learned during pre-training. This process helps optimize embeddings for particular use cases while requiring less training data than training from scratch.

- **Cool Approach:** [Qwen2-VL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.12191) - Qwen2-VL stands out due to its state-of-the-art capabilities in understanding images and videos across various resolutions and formats. The model's architecture includes Naive Dynamic Resolution and Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-ROPE), enhancing its ability to process 1D textual, 2D visual, and 3D video data. Additionally, Qwen2-VL can be integrated with devices for automated operations, making it a versatile tool for complex reasoning and decision-making tasks.

<txt><![CDATA[AHRSWORKT reports the total number of hours the respondent was at work during the previous week.  For employers and the self-employed, this includes all hours spent attending to their operation(s) or enterprise(s).  For employees, it is the number of hours they spent at work.  For unpaid family workers, it is the number of hours spent doing work directly related to the family business or farm (not including housework).
See the Hours Worked Variables Notes for an overview of the different actual and usual hours worked variables.]]></txt>

<txt><![CDATA[WKSTAT is a recode from the Census Bureau that states the part-time or full-time employment status for the respondent, and reasons.  It is derived from a number of labor force questions asked in the monthly questionnaire.]]></txt>

<txt><![CDATA[EDUC indicates respondents' educational attainment, as measured by the highest year of school or degree completed. Note that completion differs from the highest year of school attendance; for example, respondents whoÂ attendedÂ 10th grade but did not finish were classified in EDUC as havingÂ completedÂ 9th grade.Â

EDUC is a combination of two other variables, HIGRADE and EDUC99, which measure educational attainment in different ways.  HIGRADE is available for years prior to 1992 and gives the respondent's highest grade of school or year of college completed.  EDUC99 is available beginning in 1992 and classifies high school graduates according to their highest degree or diploma attained.
General and detailed codes are not yet available for IPUMS-CPS, but one can construct the general version of EDUC by reading only the first two columns of EDUC.]]></txt>

<txt><![CDATA[SCHLCOLL indicates whether respondents age 16 to 24 (or 16 to 54 for ASEC 2013 onward) were enrolled in high school or college during the previous week, and, if so, whether they were enrolled full- or part-time.  College or high school students who were currently on holiday or seasonal vacation were to answer yes, but those not taking classes during summer vacation were to answer no.  Interviewers first asked whether the person was enrolled in school during the previous week, then determined whether the person was attending high school or attending a college or university, and finally asked whether the person was a full-time or part-time student.  In IPUMS-CPS, these responses are combined into the single variable SCHLCOLL.]]></txt>
<labl>Does not attend school, college or university</labl>

<txt><![CDATA[WORKLY indicates whether or not the respondent worked any time in the calendar year previous to the survey year.  For example, if the respondent is interviewed in March of 2015, they are reporting whether they had worked any time in 2014.]]></txt>

<txt><![CDATA[WKSWORK1 reports the number of weeks, in single weeks, that the respondent worked for profit, pay, or as an unpaid family worker during the preceding calendar year.  Respondents were prompted to count weeks in which they worked for even a few hours and to include paid vacation and sick leave as work.  Information on weeks worked during the preceding year is available in the form of intervals for 1962 forward in the WKSWORK2 variable.]]></txt>

<txt><![CDATA[WKSWORK2, like WKSWORK1, reports the number of weeks that the respondent worked for profit, pay, or as an unpaid family worker during the preceding calendar year. Respondents were prompted to include weeks in which they worked for even a few hours and to include paid vacation and sick leave as work.]]></txt>

- **Fine-tuning:** A transfer learning technique that adapts pre-trained embedding models to specific domains or tasks by updating model parameters using task-specific data while preserving general knowledge learned during pre-training. DataComp addresses this shortcoming in the machine learning ecosystem by introducing a benchmark where participants can rigorously explore design decisions for datasets.  Towards this goal, we present CommonPool, a large-scale dataset with 12.8B image-text pairs collected from the web—the largest dataset of its kind by a factor of 2.5x. Embeddings are vector representations that encode semantic information from various data types, such as text, images, audio, and video.

This page outlines current approaches to embedding generation, including models, training algorithms, and benchmarks. It also covers data preparation strategies and specialized methods for domain-specific applications.
- **Trivial Approach:** Translate everything to English, then do stuff.
- **Multimodal Embedding:** Handles text, image, audio, and video.
→ **Ideal Goal:** Convert all data formats into semantic vector representations.
- Most applications require **specialized (fine-tuned)** embedding systems.*(e.g., medical embeddings: [Cohere Blog](https://cohere.com/blog/multimodal-embeddings?ref=cohere-ai.ghost.io))*

In the realm of embedding generation, various established techniques have been developed to create effective vector representations. These methods leverage different architectures, training strategies, and data types to enhance the quality and applicability of embeddings across diverse domains. Below, we explore some of the most prominent existing methods that have shaped the landscape of embedding models.

- **Contrastive Pre-training:** A self-supervised learning technique that trains models to differentiate between similar and dissimilar data pairs by maximizing the agreement between positive pairs while minimizing it for negative pairs. This approach is widely used to improve the quality of embeddings by leveraging large unlabeled datasets.

- **Fine-tuning:** A transfer learning technique that adapts pre-trained embedding models to specific domains or tasks by updating model parameters using task-specific data while preserving general knowledge learned during pre-training. This process helps optimize embeddings for particular use cases while requiring less training data than training from scratch.

- **Cool Approach:** [Qwen2-VL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.12191) - Qwen2-VL stands out due to its state-of-the-art capabilities in understanding images and videos across various resolutions and formats. It excels in visual understanding benchmarks and supports multilingual text recognition within images. The model's architecture includes Naive Dynamic Resolution and Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-ROPE), enhancing its ability to process 1D textual, 2D visual, and 3D video data. Additionally, Qwen2-VL can be integrated with devices for automated operations, making it a versatile tool for complex reasoning and decision-making tasks.
- **Clip Method:** Leverages datasets with image-caption pairs.
- **[Laion CLAP](https://huggingface.co/collections/laion/clap-contrastive-language-audio-pretraining-65415c0b18373b607262a490):** A clip-like embedding approach for audio.

It is unclear whether state-of-the-art embeddings on semantic textual similarity (STS) can be equally well applied to other tasks like clustering or reranking. This makes progress in the field difficult to track, as various models are constantly being proposed without proper evaluation. To solve this problem, we introduce the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). MTEB spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, we establish the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date. We find that no particular text embedding method dominates across all tasks. This suggests that the field has yet to converge on a universal text embedding method and scale it up sufficiently to provide state-of-the-art results on all embedding tasks. MTEB comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard at this https URL.",- [**MTEB](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.07316):**[Leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard),"# What about making our own embedding model ?
Embeddings are vector representations that encode semantic information from various data types, such as text, images, audio, and video.

This page outlines current approaches to embedding generation, including models, training algorithms, and benchmarks. It also covers data preparation strategies and specialized methods for domain-specific applications.
- **Trivial Approach:** Translate everything to English, then do stuff.
- **Multimodal Embedding:** Handles text, image, audio, and video.
→ **Ideal Goal:** Convert all data formats into semantic vector representations.
- Most applications require **specialized (fine-tuned)** embedding systems.*(e.g., medical embeddings: [Cohere Blog](https://cohere.com/blog/multimodal-embeddings?ref=cohere-ai.ghost.io))*

In the realm of embedding generation, various established techniques have been developed to create effective vector representations. These methods leverage different architectures, training strategies, and data types to enhance the quality and applicability of embeddings across diverse domains. Below, we explore some of the most prominent existing methods that have shaped the landscape of embedding models.

- **Contrastive Pre-training:** A self-supervised learning technique that trains models to differentiate between similar and dissimilar data pairs by maximizing the agreement between positive pairs while minimizing it for negative pairs. This approach is widely used to improve the quality of embeddings by leveraging large unlabeled datasets.

- **Fine-tuning:** A transfer learning technique that adapts pre-trained embedding models to specific domains or tasks by updating model parameters using task-specific data while preserving general knowledge learned during pre-training. This process helps optimize embeddings for particular use cases while requiring less training data than training from scratch.

- **Cool Approach:** [Qwen2-VL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.12191) - Qwen2-VL stands out due to its state-of-the-art capabilities in understanding images and videos across various resolutions and formats. It excels in visual understanding benchmarks and supports multilingual text recognition within images. The model's architecture includes Naive Dynamic Resolution and Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-ROPE), enhancing its ability to process 1D textual, 2D visual, and 3D video data. Additionally, Qwen2-VL can be integrated with devices for automated operations, making it a versatile tool for complex reasoning and decision-making tasks.
- **Clip Method:** Leverages datasets with image-caption pairs.
- **[Laion CLAP](https://huggingface.co/collections/laion/clap-contrastive-language-audio-pretraining-65415c0b18373b607262a490):** A clip-like embedding approach for audio.
- **Audio:** To be formatted into usable vectors.

- **AVG BEEIR**: The Average BEEIR (Balanced Embedding Evaluation and Information Retrieval) metric is designed to assess the effectiveness of embedding models in information retrieval tasks. It calculates the average precision of retrieval results across multiple queries, considering both precision and recall to provide a balanced evaluation.
